activities.caption: pair each motif with its computational job
activities.name: sbMotifMatch

config.prompt: Evolution's favourite three-node circuits — pair each with the function it performs:

pairs.left: negative autoregulation — a protein repressing its own gene
feed-forward loop (X regulates Y, both regulate Z)
pairs.right: persistence detector — a transient blip cannot trigger Z

config.why: Robust control, filtering and switching are the physics of any regulatory system — evolution, with no designer, found the same small set of designs electronic engineers reach for.

activities.anchor: the circadian clock is its showcase
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the interlocked clock loop
activities.name: sbClockCloze

config.text: CLOCK-BMAL1 activates %%0%% and CRY transcription; the PER/CRY proteins accumulate, %%1%% up, re-enter the nucleus and shut their own activation %%2%%. Slow %%3%% lets the loop run with a period of almost exactly %%4%% hours — a self-sustaining oscillator, entrained daily by light.
config.hint: The period belongs to the loop — degradation rates and delays — not to any single component.

activities.caption: file the facts — buffered or lethal
activities.name: sbOneGeneBuckets

config.prompt: Redundancy cuts both ways. File each fact:

items.label: knocking out any one component often changes nothing
synthetic lethality — two individually dispensable genes, jointly lethal
most phenotypes are distributed properties of networks
a hub whose removal collapses everything
height: hundreds of loci each contributing a sliver
the reason cancer therapy hunts for gene pairs

config.why: The gene is a part; the behaviour belongs to the wiring — which is why single-gene thinking found so few drug targets in complex disease.

activities.anchor: The models come in a ladder of ambition
activities.caption: climb the modelling ladder in order
activities.name: sbLadderOrder

config.prompt: From kinetic workhorse to endpoint demonstration — put the rungs in order:
items: ODE kinetics — write each reaction's rate and integrate (Michaelis–Menten/Hill)
Boolean networks — genes ON/OFF, logic update rules, attractor analysis
Stochastic simulation — the Gillespie algorithm samples individual reaction events
Constraint-based flux balance — stoichiometry plus optimisation, no kinetics
The 2012 whole-cell model — every known gene and reaction of one bacterium
config.why: Each rung trades detail for scale differently: coarse Boolean attractors (Kauffman's cell types), Gillespie's noise at low molecule counts, genome-scale flux models for thousands of organisms — then the whole-cell proof of concept.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the digital-human leap
activities.name: sbHumanSpot

config.prompt: This extrapolation answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Karr and colleagues (2012) simulated every known gene and reaction of Mycoplasma genitalium.
The modelled cell had 525 genes, no organelles, one cell type — about 1,900 parameters drawn from 900 papers.
A human cell runs a few thousand times more genes across hundreds of compartmentalised cell types.
Therefore a digital human cell is now within reach using the same code.
Parameters for most human reactions have never even been measured.
config.correction: The leap skips several unsolved fields — parameterisation, multiscale coupling, validation; the distance to human scale is the field's whole roadmap.
config.why: The achievement was real precisely because the organism was chosen to be small — the honest reading stops at 'a minimal bacterium is simulable in principle'.

activities.caption: raw layers vs integrated model — drag across
activities.name: sbOmicsCompare

config.prompt: Omics data, before and after integration — drag the divider:

before.label: the raw layers
before.text: RNA counts, mass-spec peaks, metabolite states — each relative and biased, batch-confounded, none readable alone.

after.label: one causal model
after.text: Layers that disagree productively, integrated: RNA abundance predicts protein abundance only weakly — and the disagreement is data.

config.why: Multi-omic integration is the field's hardest technical problem; the perturbation experiment completes the loop — models predict, perturbations judge, and the discrepancy is where the next model comes from.

activities.caption: treat the wiring — a therapy run
activities.name: sbCancerBranch

config.root: A tumour is a rewired network: oncogenes and tumour suppressors are hubs whose dysregulation propagates. Choose the therapeutic logic.

choices.label: One targeted drug against the hub
choices.feedback: Works when the tumour cannot reroute — but single-drug resistance is the norm.

choices.label: Combination therapy chosen by network analysis
choices.feedback: Hit nodes the tumour cannot reroute around at once.

choices.label: Map every protein the drug touches before trials
choices.feedback: Systems pharmacology: the off-target map predicts side effects in advance.

single.text: The network reroutes and resistance arrives — the failure mode that taught the field to combine.

combo.text: Personalised models — tumour-specific networks simulated to rank drug combinations — are in early clinical use.

pharm.text: Drugs get repurposed by network position: push the network away from a disease attractor, whatever the label.

config.why: Disease as network failure: sepsis is runaway feedback, diabetes a signalling failure, ageing interlinked hallmark pathways — the systems era treats the wiring, not a single target.

activities.anchor: Every strong systems paper is a closed loop
activities.caption: true or false — models and the bench
activities.name: sbLoopJudge

statements.s: Every strong systems paper runs a closed loop: model predicts, experiment perturbs, model revises.
statements.why: The field's actual product is the iteration.

statements.s: The 2012 whole-cell model was built from 900 primary papers and validated by new experiments.
statements.why: Bench and computation, one loop — not two tribes.

statements.s: A model that is never falsified by measurement is considered finished and publishable as-is.
statements.why: In this discipline it is considered unfinished rather than published.

statements.s: CRISPR screens are both massive wet-lab work and pure data science.
statements.why: Tens of thousands of genes perturbed in parallel, fitness read out by sequencing.
